summary: Are Usage Insights export reports audit-logged (create + download) for compliance evidence?
description:
Issue summary
Customer asked whether the new Usage Insights export flow is audit-logged in a way that is usable for compliance evidence (who exported, what filters/time range, and whether downloads are also logged).

Customer context
- Customer: Northbridge Financial (enterprise)
- Use case: FinOps / chargeback by route + internal incident/cost reviews
- Requirement: demonstrate that access to cost exports is tracked (audit trail) and that exports respect RBAC boundaries.

Questions from customer
1) Is export creation audit logged?
2) Is export download audit logged?
3) What fields are recorded (filters, time range, format, project/org, actor identity, IP)?
4) Where can an admin view/search these logs, and what is retention?

Impact
- Blocking security review sign-off for enabling exports to a wider set of internal users.

Initial notes (support)
- We believe both export creation and download are logged as discrete audit events.
- Need to confirm event names/fields, retention, and whether signed URL access is captured.

Requested from Engineering/Security
- Confirm exact audit event identifiers and required fields for compliance evidence
- Confirm whether download via console (signed URL) generates an audit event at time of download
- Provide a short support-ready answer + any doc link we can share
comments: 2026-02-11 09:12 (Dev Patel, Support) — Customer asks: “Are Usage Insights exports audit logged? We need to show who exported route-level cost reports and what filters/time range they used.” Assigning to Kevin Osei for confirmation of events/fields and to provide an approved response we can share externally.

2026-02-11 11:04 (Dev Patel, Support → Customer) — Thanks — looping in our Security/Compliance and the engineer responsible for export audit logging. We’ll confirm whether both export creation and download are logged, plus the specific fields captured (time range, filters, format, actor, etc.).

2026-02-12 14:26 (Kevin Osei, Security Eng) — Confirmed: Usage Insights exports are audit logged for both (a) export job creation and (b) report download. This is implemented in redwood PR-15492 and follows the Confluence spec “usage-report-export-audit-events”.

Details:
- Event 1: usage_insights.export_job_created
  - Emitted when a user clicks Export in the console or calls the export job creation API.
  - Includes: actor_user_id, actor_email (if available), org_id, project_id, environment, region, export_job_id, report_type (route_cost_drivers), time_range_start, time_range_end, filter_set (route/model/region/deployment_mode), format (csv|json), requested_at, client_ip, user_agent, and result (accepted|rejected + error_code).
- Event 2: usage_insights.export_report_downloaded
  - Emitted when a user downloads the report via the console download action (and also for API-based download).
  - Includes: actor_user_id, actor_email, org_id, project_id, export_job_id, format, downloaded_at, client_ip, user_agent, and bytes_sent (when available).

RBAC note: events are scoped to org/project; only users with the appropriate org role can view audit logs. Export endpoints enforce org/project isolation; audit logging does not bypass RBAC.

Retention: audit events follow our standard audit log retention policy (90 days in-console by default; longer retention available via enterprise add-on).

2026-02-12 16:01 (Naomi Feldman, Security/RBAC product review) — +1. Also note for external comms: audit logging provides evidence of access to the export artifact at download time; it cannot attest to what happens after the file is downloaded (e.g., shared externally).

2026-02-13 10:18 (Dev Patel, Support) — Draft response for customer below; please confirm wording is OK to share:

“Yes — Usage Insights export actions are audit logged. We record an audit event when an export job is created (including requesting user, org/project, time range and filters, and output format) and a separate audit event when the report is downloaded. Audit logs respect RBAC and are available to admins in the Console Audit Logs view / audit log API. Default retention is 90 days (longer retention available for enterprise).”

2026-02-13 11:02 (Kevin Osei, Security Eng) — Wording looks good. Please avoid mentioning internal event field names unless asked; but it’s OK to state we capture user identity, org/project, filters/time range, format, timestamp, and source IP/user-agent. If they need a formal spec, we can provide a redacted sample or the one-pager being tracked in INT-913.

2026-02-14 09:37 (Dev Patel, Support → Customer) — Confirmed: Usage Insights exports are audit logged.

- We write an audit event when an export is created (who initiated it, org/project scope, time range, selected filters, and requested format).
- We write a separate audit event when the report is downloaded.
- Audit logs respect RBAC (org/project boundaries) and are accessible to admins in the Console Audit Logs view and via our audit log API.
- Default retention is 90 days in-console (longer retention is available for enterprise if required).

If helpful for your security review, we can provide a redacted sample audit log entry for an export (creation + download) showing the fields captured.

2026-02-14 15:06 (Dev Patel, Support) — Customer acknowledged and requested a redacted sample. Created internal follow-up to produce a standardized one-pager + sample (INT-913). Marking ticket Resolved.
resolution: Provided confirmation that Usage Insights export creation and download are audit-logged, including the key fields captured (actor identity, org/project scope, filters/time range, format, timestamp, IP/user-agent), plus where admins can view logs and default retention. Follow-up tracked in INT-913 to provide a standardized one-pager + redacted sample audit entries for security reviews.
